limits.overflowPolicy: Reject the projection with the affected section; never silently truncate anatomy, exclusions, source IDs or retained realization.

inputContract.taxonomyPolicy: Derived classification may caption a result; it cannot supply anatomy, inherited copies, material, palette or motion.
inputContract.missingValuePolicy: Do not invent missing construction or capability values. Required projection sections report not modeled when unavailable; unresolved or rejected results cannot be sent for generation.
inputContract.facialPolicy: Eyes, mouths, noses, faces and expressions appear only when constructed nodes/surfaces explicitly provide them. Missing contributors do not establish absence of sensing, but cannot authorize facial artwork.

referencePolicy: C18 supplies crisp saturated pixel craft and optical density. Genome-field supplies clustered inspectable information lineage. Neither reference supplies subject anatomy, genotypes, resources, ability claims or a body preset.

promptSections.text: Create one appealing Critter Lab character study in the selected HiBit pixel-art direction. Give the creature a clear, memorable silhouette and a welcoming, quietly curious presence. Compose a single whole subject as the focal point, occupying roughly two thirds of the image, with comfortable clearance around every appendage. Use a simple warm dark-neutral backdrop and a restrained soft contact shadow when the supplied view supports contact. Keep the image devoted to the character, with clean open space around its silhouette.

Build the picture with crisp, deliberate pixel clusters and a consistent apparent pixel scale. Shape the silhouette with well-placed steps and nested contours; use broad calm midtone areas, compact shadow groups and small selective highlights. Concentrate detail around the leading region, declared features and important attachment transitions, then let secondary surfaces rest. Fine texture should enrich small local areas without covering every surface with repeated strokes. The subject should read immediately at thumbnail size and reward closer inspection with controlled material detail.

Portray the mapped forms as a living character study through tactile, softly modeled volumes and supple-looking surfaces. Use a warm upper-left key light with a gentle cool shadow family, keeping the actual pigment regions recognizable. Give each declared covering its own visual language: smooth skin has quiet shading; plates have readable overlapping edges; fur groups into soft directional tufts; feathers have layered vane shapes. Fine ridges use subtle low-contrast local accents. Let the supplied anatomy determine the focal point and pose; silhouette, material and composed presentation carry the character.

Use the phenotype below as the subject description. Preserve its body organization, appendage roles and rooted counts, proportion relationships, feature presence and pigment/covering fields. Illustrate those forms with confident contours and material depth rather than repeating construction glyphs. Present a quiet static pose in the supplied view, with the declared facial geometry where present. Deliver a clean raster character illustration with the artwork alone in the frame.

calibrationSheet.selectionPolicy: Use three contrasting retained resolved simulation packets from the same engine. Select by actual generated topology, surface and eligible motion, not class buttons. Include ground, air and water outputs only when their packets support those modeled motions.
calibrationSheet.composition: One compact landscape sheet with three equal columns. Each column shows the same subject in a clear neutral construction view and, only when supported, one declared action pose. Keep ample separation and coherent apparent scale/pixel density. No baked text; record subject IDs and panel order in the retained manifest.
calibrationSheet.evidenceLimit: A sheet is concept calibration and semantic inspection. It does not supply individual sprite exports, coherent motion frames, a rig, exact native dimensions or production approval.

mustCheck: shared pixel craft without shared anatomy
review.repairPolicy: One focused correction addresses concrete defects. A second failed round requires diagnosing framing with the coordinator before another generation or broader work.
